contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #117: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps.

Degree-d correction for the complete-line test on any finite vector space under a scalar-invariant direction law and an explicit internal-edge estimate; the matrix-walk spectral premise is not inferred from correction.

definitions.line_failure: P restricted to all q points A+t h is not represented by a univariate polynomial of degree at most d
definitions.internal_edge: For every nonempty E, Pr[x+h in E | x uniform in E,h distributed as D] is at most mu(E)+lambda

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 117 (Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps.; papers: Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut; Near-square-root logarithmic integrality gaps for uniform sparsest cut; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/117.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

For every fixed C>1 there is a polynomial-time 3CNF-to-rational-capacity uniform-sparsest-cut reduction with SAT optimum at most a and UNSAT optimum greater than C a, with unit demand on every distinct pair. Source: hardness sections/00-introduction.tex, thm:main.

The characteristic-two tower simple-pole lemma gives irreducibility of X^r+X-b, the local basis, ramification order r, and discriminant order 2(r-1). Source: hardness sections/01-pencil.tex, lem:pencil-simple-pole.

For fixed lambda_0>0 and sufficiently large power-of-two r, q=r^2, every d>=1 has a deterministic 2^{O(d)}-time list of m=O(d) vectors containing the standard basis; every homogeneous quadratic nonzero on the list vanishes on at most lambda_0 m list indices. Source: lem:pencil.

The actual rank-one matrix walk has mean-zero L2 norm at most lambda_1=lambda_0+q^{-1}; hence every nonempty E has conditional internal directed edge probability at most mu(E)+lambda_1. Source: sections/02-bit-tests.tex, lem:matrix-walk and eq:internal-edge-bound.
The four-time masked parity law is exchangeable with uniform marginals and pair norm at most max(lambda_1,2/(q-3)), with the same bound on two independent copies. Source: lem:masked-pair-mixing.

Products of principal minors vanishing on Boolean diagonals admit the displayed minor-product slack; tag-bank and selector differences pack the honest fields while preserving quadratic rank-one line restrictions. Source: lem:minor-product-slack and eq:selector-isolation.

With gamma=10^{-3}, line failure at most delta^2, 2delta+lambda_1<gamma/2, 1-4gamma-4delta-2/(q-1)>delta+lambda_1, and 27gamma+5delta<1, there exist one scalar-invariant H of direction mass at least 1-delta and one P' differing on at most 2delta, quadratic on every H-line at every base. Source: lem:quadratic-correction.
A nonzero function of degree at most D<q-1 on scalar-invariant directions of mass at least 1-rho has support density at least 1-rho-D/(q-1)-lambda_1. Source: lem:line-support-gap.

After correction, subgroup stabilizers exactify assignment invariance and bank affinity; fixed-shift expansion bounds full discrepancy degree by four; the support gap forces exact identities and gives a satisfying Boolean assignment. Source: sections/02-bit-tests.tex, Support gaps and exact bank affinity.

For each fixed lambda>0, polynomially enumerable bounded-arity bit tests have bounded marginals, perfect completeness, constant soundness, and a mixing exchangeable four-bit parity law. Source: thm:bit-test-system.

A valuation with the manuscript's approximate calibration and order-preservation properties yields a satisfying Boolean assignment through the bit-test system. Source: sections/03-events.tex, lem:event-obstruction.

The rare-event criterion extracts the required calibrated valuation from the manuscript's conjunction-response hypothesis without dependence on minimum atom or support size. Source: sections/04-entropy.tex, lem:rare-event.

The analytic score-gap theorem links bounded score functions, comparison cost, and demand variance to the valuation obstruction; its amplitude signal is transferred through the path argument. Source: sections/05-scores.tex, thm:score-gap and lem:amplitude-signal.
The conditional-kernel and ordered-path estimates establish the finite score-compilation interface. Source: sections/06-paths.tex, prop:score-compilation.

Rational score rounding, key replication, and heavy/auxiliary edges yield unit demand on every distinct pair while preserving the promised completeness and all-nontrivial-cuts soundness ratio. Source: sections/07-finite-graph.tex, lem:rational-compilation and eq:final-threshold.

There are c>0 and uniform-demand instances on n_j tending to infinity with positive Goemans-Linial optimum and OPT/GL >= c sqrt(log n_j)/(log log n_j)^3. This is an existential integrality-gap sequence, not computational hardness. Source: gap main.tex, thm:main.
For N=m^6 and S=m^3 the direction charts satisfy norm, covariance, Gaussian-approximation, and uniform directional-maximum controls. Source: gap directions.tex, lem:directions.
The kernel construction with a=m^{-40}, b=m^{40}, epsilon=m^{-200}, r=m^{-8}, tau=m^{-2000} supplies the stated global and local angle controls. Source: gap kernel.tex, ker:parameters and ker:angles.
Triangle repair produces a negative-type semimetric, preserves macroscopic distances, and controls adjacent rounded-label distances. Source: gap repair.tex, lem:repair.

The finite negative-type metric has macroscopic distance c_*sqrt(m)|theta-eta| up to Cr, same-chart adjacent bound C tau(m/N)(log m)^2, size at most exp(Cm log m), diameter at most Cm, and first-chart average at least cm. Source: gap metric.tex, prop:metric.
Every finite-dimensional l1 contraction of the constructed metric has first-chart average distance at most C sqrt(m)(log m)^{5/2}. Source: gap contraction.tex, prop:contraction.

For a squared-Hilbert semimetric with mean at least a and every finite-dimensional l1 contraction having mean at most b, cut-cone duality gives capacities with OPT>=1 and 0<GL<=b/a. Source: gap reduction.tex, lem:duality.

Multiplicity rounding M=m^m+m^2|V| and k_v=1+floor(Mw_v) makes uniform copies with TV error <=m^{-2}, mean metric >=c'm and contraction mean <=C'sqrt(m)(log m)^{5/2}. Source: gap reduction.tex, red:tv, red:uniform-metric and red:uniform-contraction.
The uniform-copy gap is at least c''sqrt(m)/(log m)^{5/2} and m log m<=log n<=Km log m, yielding the stated sqrt(log n)/(log log n)^3 sequence. Source: gap reduction.tex, red:m-gap and red:size.

Markov's inequality and internal-edge expansion produce one missing set of density <=2epsilon/alpha, containing all points whose bad-direction mass exceeds alpha, with every assigned point entering the missing set with probability <gamma.

Under the generalized theorem hypotheses, every degree-d interpolation relation in a good direction whose d+2 positions avoid the cleaned missing set is exact; a nonempty failure set would have internal-edge probability greater than beta+lambda.

With r=d+1 interpolation nodes and missing-entry bound gamma, a modal prediction has collision failure <=(r^2+2r)gamma+2rho; peeling and a single common transverse-direction event preserve every newly enabled relation when (2r^2+3r)gamma+3rho<1, without a union bound over relations or dimension.

With gamma=10^{-3}, line failure at most delta^2, 2delta+lambda_1<gamma/2, 1-4gamma-4delta-2/(q-1)>delta+lambda_1, and 27gamma+5delta<1, there exist one scalar-invariant H of direction mass at least 1-delta and one P' differing on at most 2delta, quadratic on every H-line at every base. import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Argus9000117

theorem weighted_grid_comm
    {I J R : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [CommRing R]
    (a : I → R) (b : J → R) (z : I → J → R) :
    (∑ i, a i * ∑ j, b j * z i j) =
      ∑ j, b j * ∑ i, a i * z i j := by
  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  ring

theorem grid_predictions_agree
    {I J R : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [CommRing R]
    (a : I → R) (b : J → R) (z : I → J → R)
    (u : I → R) (v : J → R)
    (hu : ∀ i, u i = ∑ j, b j * z i j)
    (hv : ∀ j, v j = ∑ i, a i * z i j) :
    (∑ i, a i * u i) = ∑ j, b j * v j := by
  calc
    (∑ i, a i * u i) = ∑ i, a i * ∑ j, b j * z i j := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [hu i]
    _ = ∑ j, b j * ∑ i, a i * z i j := weighted_grid_comm a b z
    _ = ∑ j, b j * v j := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      rw [hv j]

theorem translated_relations_transfer
    {I J R : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [CommRing R]
    (c : I → R) (b : J → R) (z : I → J → R)
    (v : I → R)
    (hv : ∀ i, v i = ∑ j, b j * z i j)
    (hz : ∀ j, ∑ i, c i * z i j = 0) :
    ∑ i, c i * v i = 0 := by
  calc
    (∑ i, c i * v i) = ∑ i, c i * ∑ j, b j * z i j := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _
      rw [hv i]
    _ = ∑ j, b j * ∑ i, c i * z i j := weighted_grid_comm c b z
    _ = 0 := by simp [hz]

theorem collision_le_modal
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I]
    (p : I → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hs : ∑ i, p i = 1)
    (m : I) (hm : ∀ i, p i ≤ p m) :
    (∑ i, (p i) ^ 2) ≤ p m := by
  calc
    (∑ i, (p i) ^ 2) ≤ ∑ i, p m * p i := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i _
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg (hp i) (sub_nonneg.mpr (hm i))]
    _ = p m := by rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hs, mul_one]

theorem modal_mass_from_collision
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I]
    (p : I → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hs : ∑ i, p i = 1)
    (eta : ℝ) (hc : 1 - eta ≤ ∑ i, (p i) ^ 2) :
    ∃ m, (∀ i, p i ≤ p m) ∧ 1 - eta ≤ p m := by
  obtain ⟨m, _, hm⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_max_image (Finset.univ : Finset I) p Finset.univ_nonempty
  have hmax : ∀ i, p i ≤ p m := fun i => hm i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  exact ⟨m, hmax, hc.trans (collision_le_modal p hp hs m hmax)⟩

theorem collision_budget (r gamma rho : ℝ) :
    (r + r) * gamma + (r * r) * gamma + 2 * rho =
      (r ^ 2 + 2 * r) * gamma + 2 * rho := by ring

theorem shared_direction_completion_budget (r gamma rho : ℝ) :
    ((r ^ 2 + 2 * r) * gamma + 2 * rho) +
        rho + (r * (r + 1)) * gamma =
      (2 * r ^ 2 + 3 * r) * gamma + 3 * rho := by ring

theorem quadratic_specialization (gamma rho : ℝ) :
    (2 * (3 : ℝ) ^ 2 + 3 * 3) * gamma + 3 * rho =
      27 * gamma + 3 * rho := by ring

theorem manuscript_completion_implies_improved
    (gamma delta : ℝ) (hd : 0 ≤ delta)
    (h : 27 * gamma + 5 * delta < 1) :
    27 * gamma + 3 * delta < 1 := by linarith

theorem manuscript_cleanup_margin
    (delta lambda : ℝ)
    (hd : delta ≤ 1 / 16000) (hl : lambda ≤ 1 / 1000000) :
    (187 : ℝ) / 500000 ≤ 1 / 2000 - 2 * delta - lambda := by
  linarith

theorem nonvacuity_numerator_identities (s : ℝ) :
    192 * (s + 1) ^ 2 + 271 * (s + 1) - 22 =
        192 * s ^ 2 + 655 * s + 441 ∧
      224 * (s + 1) ^ 2 + 336 * (s + 1) - 3 =
        224 * s ^ 2 + 784 * s + 557 := by
  constructor <;> ring

theorem all_degree_margins_positive
    (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    0 < (192 * r ^ 2 + 271 * r - 22) /
        (128 * (2 * r ^ 2 + 3 * r)) ∧
      0 < (224 * r ^ 2 + 336 * r - 3) /
        (128 * (2 * r ^ 2 + 3 * r)) := by
  have hc : 0 < 2 * r ^ 2 + 3 * r := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg r]
  have hden : 0 < 128 * (2 * r ^ 2 + 3 * r) := by positivity
  constructor
  · apply div_pos _ hden
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (r - 1)]
  · apply div_pos _ hden
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (r - 1)]

end Argus9000117

claims.natural_statement: Under the input hypotheses of Q_GENERAL, not its correction conclusion, Markov's inequality and 2epsilon/alpha+lambda<gamma/2 produce one missing set of density <=2epsilon/alpha, containing all points whose bad-direction mass exceeds alpha, with every outside point entering the missing set with probability <gamma.

Under the input hypotheses of Q_GENERAL, not its correction conclusion, define H by failing-base fraction <=beta and take the cleaned set from Q_CLEANUP. Every degree-d interpolation relation in an H direction whose d+2 positions are clean is exact; a nonempty failure set would have internal-edge probability greater than beta+lambda.

Under the input hypotheses of Q_GENERAL, not its correction conclusion, let fixed scalar-invariant H have missing direction mass <=rho and let a partial assignment satisfy every H interpolation relation on old assigned points. With r=d+1 nonzero interpolation nodes, assigned-point entry into the missing set <=gamma, and a missing center with the same entry bound, a modal prediction has collision failure <=(r^2+2r)gamma+2rho. One common transverse-direction event for each newly enabled relation extends the partial assignment at that center when (2r^2+3r)gamma+3rho<1, preserving all relations and entry bounds after removal of that center, without a union bound over relations or dimension.
